correctness.rationale: Any two white vertices in one independent fibre have identical external neighborhoods and form a fort, so the first of them cannot be forced. With at most one white representative per fibre and m≥2, every fibre always contains a blue vertex. Each such vertex sees exactly one white neighbor iff its base vertex sees exactly one white base neighbor, independently of whether that base vertex is blue. This gives a stepwise correspondence, including isolated base vertices, and a labelled bijection with pairs consisting of a skew-forcing set F and one omitted label per fibre outside F. The weight is m^(n-|F|) z^(n(m-1)+|F|). Deleting a selected vertex in a partial fibre fails the fort condition; deleting one in a full fibre removes the associated vertex from F. Since forcing is upward closed, the single-deletion test suffices for minimality. The two substitutions, equality for Z, and minimum/minimal-size consequences follow. On C_n the two neighbors of i are i-1 and i+1, so every force crosses a step-two edge between these neighbors; a component is occupied exactly when seeded. The proof's phrase 'cyclic distance two' must be understood as step ±2 mod n: for n=3 the two neighbors are adjacent and the step graph is C3, and for n=4 it is two K2 components. The formulas as stated therefore hold also at both small n. Counting seed choices by parity gives the displayed polynomials and minimum counts. Base rotations and fibre swaps give transitivity; n≥5 yields connected triangle-free 4-regular graphs with 4n edges and the claimed exponential counts. I inspected verify.cpp, not executed uploaded code. It checks finite cases by a shared closure routine with separate ordinary/skew eligibility, not two separately written closure algorithms; the analytical argument, not finite agreement, proves the universal statement.

value.rationale: The transfer is structural and all-graphs: it relates ordinary and skew forcing without losing labelled enumerators or inclusion-minimal sets. This is stronger and more reusable than a scalar product bound. The cycle application connects it directly to an explicit question and retains degree four, connectivity and vertex-transitivity while achieving exponentially many minimal sets, with all such sets simultaneously minimum. These features motivate both the independent-fibre operation and the choice of cycle bases.
